Where to find the VIN on a VW, Audi, Seat or Škoda, and how to check it

Updated 12 November 2026

The VIN is on the plate under the windscreen, the vehicle data sticker in the boot, the stamping in the engine bay and the type plate, and many control units store it too. All of them should show the same 17 characters as the registration certificate. A control unit with another VIN usually means a used part; markings that disagree point to a changed identity.

Where the VIN is marked

Check every marking, not just the one under the windscreen, and compare each with the registration certificate.

MarkingWhere to look
Windscreen plateLower corner of the windscreen, readable from outside.
Vehicle data stickerSpare-wheel well or boot floor; a copy is in the service booklet.
Body stampingEngine bay bulkhead or front strut tower; on some models under the passenger floor.
Type plateB-pillar or engine bay.
Registration certificateThe car’s legal identity, the reference for all the others.

While you look, watch for grinding, filler, fresh paint or welds near the stamping, characters that are not aligned, a scratched, glued or re-riveted plate, or a missing or reprinted sticker.

How to read a VW-group VIN

A VIN has 17 characters. On a car built for Europe by the Volkswagen group it reads like WVWZZZ1KZ9P409108.

PositionExampleMeaning
1–3WVWMaker: WVW Volkswagen cars, WV1 and WV2 Volkswagen vans, WAU Audi, WUA Audi Sport (RS models), VSS Seat, TMB Škoda. Cars built outside Europe can start differently.
4–6ZZZFiller on European cars.
7–81KModel code, for example 1K Golf 5, 5K Golf 6, AU Golf 7, 8P and 8V Audi A3, 8K Audi A4, 4F Audi A6, 1Z and 5E Octavia, 1P and 5F Leon.
9ZFiller (a check digit on cars for North America).
109Model year: 1–9 for 2001–2009, then A 2010, B 2011, C 2012, D 2013, E 2014, F 2015, G 2016, H 2017, J 2018, K 2019, L 2020, M 2021, N 2022, P 2023, R 2024, S 2025, T 2026.
11PFactory.
12–17409108Serial number.

The model year often starts in the summer of the previous calendar year, so it can differ from the first registration date by one.

Check the VIN the control units store

The markings are the car’s visible identity. Many control units also store the VIN of the car they were adapted to: the engine, the immobiliser, the cluster, the airbag unit and others. Reading them over the OBD socket shows whether the electronics belong to the same car as the body.

With VAG Scope, the VIN check reads the VIN from every unit that answers, lets you confirm each marking you checked, and lists what it found.

FindingWhat it usually meansWhat to do
Markings show different VINsA car has one VIN everywhere: a changed identity, or a misread.Read them again and compare with the registration certificate. If they still differ, contact the police or the registration authority.
Units belong to another VINVisible markings can be copied; control units keep the identity they were adapted to.Compare with the registration certificate, then contact the police or the registration authority.
An identity unit from another carThe immobiliser or engine unit is adapted to the car when fitted. Another VIN means a used, unadapted unit or a partly changed identity.Ask for the invoice, have the car checked by a dealer or an expert.
An airbag unit from another carDeployed airbags call for a new airbag unit. A used one points to a cheap crash repair.Ask about accidents and have the repair inspected.
Other units from another carCommon after repairs with used parts (radio, navigation, comfort unit).Usually harmless. A cluster from another car means its odometer began on that car.

The check also counts the keys the immobiliser has learned. If more keys are learned than you were given, one may be in someone else’s hands: ask for all of them, or have a dealer relearn the keys so missing ones stop working.

What a VIN check cannot prove

  • VINs can be rewritten with workshop tools. A car rewritten everywhere looks consistent.
  • Many units store no VIN, and older cars may hold it in only two or three.
  • The maker’s online records, dealer history and immobiliser secrets are not read.
  • Units that do not answer, engine and gearbox numbers and body panels are not checked.

A unit with another car’s VIN is common after a repair with used parts and shows nothing illegal. Matching VINs do not show that a car is not stolen. If in doubt, ask the police or the registration authority, and never accuse anyone on the basis of this result alone.

Then check the mileage

If the cluster came from another car, its odometer did not start with this one. Read the mileage check guide with that in mind.

Run the check on your own car

VAG Scope does it from your phone and a Bluetooth ELM327 adapter: no account, no network, and every result shows its evidence.
